name: Hollowfield Cycle Workshop

do: Name the part and the measurement
Say what a job will not fix
Say who does the work and at which bench
Prefer the trade word to the marketing word
dont: Never use the phrase 'the ride of your life'
Never write about lifestyle, freedom, adventure or wellbeing
Never quote or imply a price for work before the bike has been seen
Never call the workshop passionate, artisanal or boutique
Never describe a job as quick, easy or effortless
Never address the reader as a cyclist tribe ('fellow riders', 'the peloton')
Never promise that a service will fix something it does not cover

offerings.name: Winter Service Plan
features: Chain wear measured and reported each visit
offerings.description: A quarterly strip-down through the salt season: drivetrain cleaned and measured, cables replaced, brakes bled, bearings checked.

offerings.name: Hand-Built Wheelset
features: Rim and hub chosen with the rider
Tension chart supplied with the build
One free re-true after the first month
offerings.description: A pair of wheels laced and tensioned by hand on our own bench, built to the rider's weight and the roads they ride.

positioning: For year-round commuters and audax riders who put real mileage on one bike, Hollowfield is the two-bench arch where the worn part is measured, named and quoted in writing before a spanner touches anything — the opposite of a three-week queue and a bike handed back with the same drivetrain on it.

composition_plan.intent: Open on the first row of the spec split rather than a pitch: name the workshop and where it stands, with one visual field holding the arch interior. Narrow column carries the identifying label, wide column the plain statement of what happens here.
State the failure this workshop exists against, set large, with the narrow detail column qualifying it in flat specifics so the claim reads as observation rather than complaint.
Make the sequence from drop-off to inspection to written quote to handback legible before anyone books, so the process itself is the reassurance. The ordered list supplies the numbering.
Set what is sold side by side, one column per offering, with each offering's exclusions visible inside its own column rather than buried below the table.
One row per bench practice, each carrying a single idea about measurement, wear or tolerance; the rows flip which side is narrow so the rule between columns walks down the page.
A band of the given figures under short labels so scale and standing are stated flatly and no reader has to infer them.
Answer the questions a rider asks before handing over a bike: what a quote covers, what it deliberately does not, how long the bike stays.
Address, phone and email, and nothing else — the closing row of the specification sheet.
